posts.title: Six Conversations on Research, Methods, Ethics and Academic Life
posts.description: I was interviewed by Szymon Chrzątowski , a researcher from Poland, for six short posts on Facebook about research, research methods, ethics and academic life. Reading them afterwards got me thinking about things that come up in different parts of my work. There is a fair amount of overlap between writing books, teaching, organising a conference and doing research myself. Also not everyone is on Facebook (I’m not!) so I thought I would summarise the posts here. The first post was about independent research. I have been a researcher for more than 25 years and have never been employed by a university. People are often surprised by this. They ask if you can really have a research career outside academia, and you can, although there are difficulties as well as benefits. You have freedom to choose your work, but financial security is more difficult. For me, being able to choose my projects and follow the questions I am interested in is most important. posts.title: Ten Top Tips for Becoming an Inclusive Presenter
posts.description: Think about who will be in your audience and what their access needs might be. If you’re struggling to figure this out, look at the conference website and, if relevant, the website(s) of any associated organisation(s). If that doesn’t help (or doesn’t help enough), ask the conference organisers what kinds of people usually attend and what their access needs may be. This kind of preparation is important and useful, but it won’t necessarily inform you about everyone’s access needs, so don’t assume you know them all even if the audience is very familiar to you. Encourage people to move around, stim, take breaks in a quieter space, or do whatever else they can to meet their own needs. This might mean someone with back pain standing rather than sitting; a neurodivergent person crafting or stimming with a fidget toy; someone needing to leave the room for a short while to take an urgent call. posts.title: How To Create An Inclusive Conference
posts.description: From the very start, our aim for the International Creative Research Methods Conference was to make it an inclusive conference. We have mostly managed that – and learned a load of lessons along the way. So I thought I would share some of those with you. First, you need an inclusive venue. We are very lucky with the studio… in central Manchester, UK, who work hard to be accessible for people with disabilities, neurodivergence, special dietary needs, parents with babies or older children. Everyone is welcome and everyone is catered for, including lived experience researchers. In our first year we had a mix-up over hearing loops. These are essential to have for anyone who may be d/Deaf or hearing-impaired, and we knew that, but we thought they were provided automatically. In fact you have to request them, something we have done every year since. So, even with an inclusive venue, read the Ts and Cs!
